lyrics:
[Intro: slow piano chords, distant sirens, soft choir]

[Chorus: male tenor, sung, piano and choir]
Sing it for the corner, sing it for the block
Sing it for the boys who never heard the clock
Lay it down, lay it down
Before the candles and the flowers on the ground
Sing it for the corner now

[Verse 1: male rap, urgent, older voice]
I stood right there in ninety-four with something in my coat
Seventeen and certain, with a lump inside my throat
Somebody's grandma called me by my government name
Said, "Your mother raised you better." Lord, the shame.
I walked. That's all I did. I walked. I'm here.
Half the boys I stood with never saw another year
So when I pull up slow and roll the window, that ain't hate
I'm somebody's grandma now. I'm telling you: it ain't too late.

[Chorus: male tenor, sung, piano and choir]
Sing it for the corner, sing it for the block
Sing it for the boys who never heard the clock
Lay it down, lay it down
Before the candles and the flowers on the ground
Sing it for the corner now

[Verse 2: rap, pleading, strings in]
You think nobody sees you. I see you. I was you.
You think there ain't a door. I'll walk you through.
Got a shop that needs a hand, got a cousin with a truck
It's slow money. Slow money don't get you shot up.
Your little sister's watching from the window on the third
She's gonna be whatever she just saw and what she heard
I can't make you. I can stand here. I can ask.
I can come back tomorrow. I ain't got a harder task.

[Bridge: choir alone, hushed]
Mothers, sing it
Fathers, sing it
While they're here to hear it

[Final Chorus: tenor and full choir]
Sing it for the corner, sing it for the block
Sing it for the boys who never heard the clock
Lay it down, lay it down
Before the candles and the flowers on the ground
Sing it for the corner now

[Outro: piano, a car door, footsteps walking away together]
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 80 BPM, 4/4, G minor. Slow, pleading and tender, a piano ballad with a heavy beat.

VOICE: The rapper is an older man, husky and urgent, pressing every line. The chorus is sung by a clear, emotional male tenor in a 1970s singer-songwriter style, joined by a gospel choir.

INSTRUMENTS: A grand piano playing slow, rolling chords, a deep kick and a crisp snare, a warm bass guitar, a string section, a gospel choir, a little acoustic guitar, street sounds at the ends.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro, piano and sirens. 0:16 Chorus 1. 0:46 Verse 1. 1:32 Chorus 2. 2:02 Verse 2. 2:48 Bridge, choir. 3:02 Final chorus. 3:32 Outro, a car door and footsteps, ends 3:48.

PRODUCTION & MIX: Mid-2000s rap ballad: polished, wide and emotional, piano and tenor bright, drums heavy underneath.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: 'I'm somebody's grandma now. I'm telling you: it ain't too late.' at 1:26.

MODERN POINT OF VIEW: The original is a young man pleading from inside the danger. This is one of the few who walked away, thirty years on, coming back to the same corner to say so.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Remembering, ashamed, pleading, staying.
